exposure: familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) attacks during pregnancy
cohort: The study included 89 FMF patients with a history of at least one pregnancy.
finding: Presence of FMF attacks during pregnancy was associated with an increased risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs) and neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admissions, with attacks in the second and third trimesters being significantly linked to APOs.
mod_finding: A higher number of caesarean sections was an independent predictor of neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) admission.
